# spire-entry-reader

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from services/spire-entry-reader/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/spire-entry-reader.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `spire-entry-reader` component of `services/spire-entry-reader`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.spire.reader`: generated from its catalogue, spire-entry-reader.json, by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `SPIRE_ENTRY_READER` (components).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_SOCKET` | `/tmp/spire-server/private/api.sock`; a file path | SPIRE Server's API socket (the server's socket_path): the reader opens it to call CountEntries, ListEntries and GetEntry, and nothing else. Whoever can open it can also create entries under SPIRE's default policy, so the socket's owner and group are the access control, not the mount | **Per request**: A socket that is missing or that this process cannot open: every read answers 503 spire_unavailable with Retry-After: 1, and /health answers 503 | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_TRUST_DOMAIN` | Unset | The SPIRE Server's trust domain, such as example.org: the only one whose SPIFFE ids the reader looks up. An id in another trust domain is refused with 400 before SPIRE is asked | **Doesn't start**: Unset, or not a trust domain name (lower-case letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores): the reader does not start, naming it | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_PORT` | `8443`; a whole number, 1 to 65535 | The port the reader serves HTTPS on | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 1 to 65535: the reader does not start | Any | No |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_TLS_CERT_FILE` | Unset; a file path | The reader's own certificate chain, PEM, leaf first. Read again when the file changes (checked every 60 s), so a certificate manager can rotate it without a restart | **Doesn't start**: Unset or unreadable, or not matching the key: the reader does not start. A replacement that fails to read or does not match the key is refused at the next check with an ERROR, and the reader keeps serving the certificate it has | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_TLS_KEY_FILE` | Unset; a file path | The private key for OIDF_SPIRE_READER_TLS_CERT_FILE, an unencrypted PKCS#8 key in PEM, EC or RSA; read again with the certificate | **Doesn't start**: Unset, unreadable, encrypted or not PKCS#8: the reader does not start; at a later check the old pair stays in use, with an ERROR | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_CLIENT_CA_FILE` | Unset; a file path | The certificate authorities, PEM, a client certificate must chain to. Every request needs a client certificate (mutual TLS); one that does not chain to these fails the handshake. Read once at start | **Doesn't start**: Unset, unreadable or holding no certificate: the reader does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_CLIENT_SPKI_SHA256` | Unset; a list | The clients allowed, by the SHA-256 of the client certificate's public key (SubjectPublicKeyInfo), base64url without padding or hex, space- or comma-separated; list two while PingFederate's key rotates. Unset, any certificate from OIDF_SPIRE_READER_CLIENT_CA_FILE is served, which production refuses: a certificate the same authority issued to another system would be enough | **Doesn't start**: An entry that is not a SHA-256 in base64url or hex: the reader does not start. A client whose key is not listed gets 403 forbidden_client | Required in production | Yes |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS` | `2000`; milliseconds, 100 to 10000 | The deadline on each call to SPIRE Server, in milliseconds | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 100 to 10000: the reader does not start. A call that runs past it answers 503 spire_unavailable | Any | No |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_MAX_ENTRIES` | `64`; a whole number, 1 to 256 | The most registration entries one SPIFFE id may have before the reader refuses to answer for it (502 too_many_entries), checked against CountEntries before listing and again while paging | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 1 to 256: the reader does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE` | `600`; a whole number, 1 to 60000 | Requests each client may make per minute, counted per client key in this process's memory (a token bucket): a refused request gets 429 rate_limited with Retry-After. Each reader counts on its own; there is no shared count | **Doesn't start**: Not a whole number from 1 to 60000: the reader does not start | Any | Yes |
| `OIDF_SPIRE_READER_TLS12` | `false` | Whether a client may use TLS 1.2 as well as 1.3, for a development client that cannot do 1.3 | **Doesn't start**: Not true or false: the reader does not start. True under the production profile: the reader does not start | Not in production: `true` | Yes |
| `sun.net.httpserver.maxReqTime` (system property) | `5`; a whole number, 1 to 60 | The JDK HTTP server's own limit, in seconds, from a connection's first byte to a whole request; the reader sets it to 5 unless the JVM was started with it, so a connection that stalls in the TLS handshake or the request line is closed and frees its worker (README, Threat model) | **Not checked**: The JDK reads it, not the reader: zero or less turns the limit off, and then a few connections that stall before a whole request hold every worker for good; a large value lets them hold the workers that long | Any | Yes |
